# Protocol Synopsis — RETRO-03 (retrospective, as-of 2014-04-29)

**Title:** First-in-Human Phase 1 Study of DV-R03 in Patients with Advanced Cancer (retrospective review input)
**Sponsor:** masked · **Countries:** United States · **Phase:** 1

## Investigational Product
DV-R03 is an oral small molecule (ALK tyrosine kinase receptor inhibitor). SMILES: Cc1cc(Nc2ncc(Cl)c(Nc3ccccc3S(=O)(=O)C(C)C)n2)c(OC(C)C)cc1C1CCNCC1. Target: ALK.

## Source of This Synopsis
This synopsis was assembled from the published results of the first-in-human Phase 1 study (published 2014), before regulatory approval.
Drug and sponsor code names are masked as DV-R03. No other protocol text is available. The dose selected for later development is the dose under review.

## Phase 1 Study Report (published abstract, verbatim except masking)
Background: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the anaplastic lymphoma kinase gene (ALK) rearrangement is sensitive to the ALK inhibitor crizotinib, but resistance invariably develops. DV-R03 (DV-R03) is a new ALK inhibitor that has shown greater antitumor potency than crizotinib in preclinical studies.

Methods: In this phase 1 study, we administered oral DV-R03 in doses of 50 to 750 mg once daily to patients with advanced cancers harboring genetic alterations in ALK. In an expansion phase of the study, patients received the maximum tolerated dose. Patients were assessed to determine the safety, pharmacokinetic properties, and antitumor activity of DV-R03. Tumor biopsies were performed before DV-R03 treatment to identify resistance mutations in ALK in a group of patients with NSCLC who had had disease progression during treatment with crizotinib.

Results: A total of 59 patients were enrolled in the dose-escalation phase. The maximum tolerated dose of DV-R03 was 750 mg once daily; dose-limiting toxic events included diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, elevated aminotransferase levels, and hypophosphatemia. This phase was followed by an expansion phase, in which an additional 71 patients were treated, for a total of 130 patients overall. Among 114 patients with NSCLC who received at least 400 mg of DV-R03 per day, the overall response rate was 58% (95% confidence interval [CI], 48 to 67). Among 80 patients who had received crizotinib previously, the response rate was 56% (95% CI, 45 to 67). Responses were observed in patients with various resistance mutations in ALK and in patients without detectable mutations. Among patients with NSCLC who received at least 400 mg of DV-R03 per day, the median progression-free survival was 7.0 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.5).

Conclusions: DV-R03 was highly active in patients with advanced, ALK-rearranged NSCLC, including those who had had disease progression during crizotinib treatment, regardless of the presence of resistance mutations in ALK.

둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_008.quote:
The background information for each expansion cohort should contain its scientific rationale. 
Information supporting individual expansion cohorts should describe the prespecified stopping 
rules for that cohort, based on insufficient antitumor activity or unacceptable level of toxicity for 
that population. Finally, the analysis plan for each expansion cohort should contain adequate 
information justifying the planned sample size based on the cohort objectives. For those cohorts 
evaluating antitumor activity, the plans should specify the magnitude of antitumor activity that 
would warrant further evaluation of the drug, for example by specifying the precision and power 
considerations for detection of clinically meaningful antitumor activity. In general, in a 
nonrandomized cohort, assessment of antitumor activity is determined using a Simon two-stage 
design or other designs (e.g., Bayesian statistical design) to limit exposure of additional subjects 
to a potentially ineffective drug.24

ev_009.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_009.quote:
The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-
based approach to quality management , which involves incorporating quality into the design 
of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports).

ev_010.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_010.quote:
Risk control should be proportionate to the importance of the risk to participant s’ 
rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of trial results. Risk mitigation 
activities may be incorporated, for example, in protocol design and implementation, 
monitoring plans, agreements between parties defining roles and responsibilities, and 
training.  
Where relevant, the sponsor should set pre-specified acceptable ranges (e.g., quality 
tolerance limits at the tr ial level) to support the control of risks 
to critical to quality factors. These pre -specified ranges reflect limits that when 
exceeded have the potential to impact participant safety or the reliability of trial 
results. Where deviation beyond these ranges is detected , an evaluation should be 
performed to determine if there is a possible systemic issue and if action is needed.

prescription drugs3 or biological products for the treatment of oncologic diseases during clinical 
development and prior to submitting an application for approval of a new indication and usage.   
This guidance should be considered along with the International Conference on Harmonisation

1994) when identifying an optimized dosage(s).4

ev_024.document_title: Expansion Cohorts: Use in First-in-Human Clinical Trials to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics
ev_024.section: A Assessing Safety of Recommended Phase 2 Dose
ev_024.quote:
Expansion cohorts can be intended to further evaluate safety beyond the initial dose-escalation 
portion of a trial. These studies should be supported by detailed information on available safety 
and PK data from the dose-escalation phase and a summary of safety data from other expansion 
cohorts, if available. In situations when there is a narrow therapeutic index and dose-limiting 
toxicities have been observed in the dose escalation phase that may be fatal or result in serious 
morbidity, FDA strongly recommends that expansion be delayed until sufficient data are 
available to determine the recommended phase 2 dose to help ensure subjects safety.

ev_026.document_title: Expansion Cohorts: Use in First-in-Human Clinical Trials to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics
ev_026.quote:
The purpose of this guidance is to provide advice to sponsors regarding the design and conduct 
of first-in-human (FIH) clinical trials intended to efficiently expedite the clinical development of 
oncology drugs, including biological products, through multiple expansion cohort trial designs.2 
These are trial designs that employ multiple, concurrently accruing subject cohorts, where 
individual cohorts assess different aspects of the safety, pharmacokinetics, and antitumor activity 
of the drug product.  
This guidance provides FDA’s current thinking regarding (1) characteristics of drug products 
best suited for consideration for development under a multiple expansion cohort trial; (2) 
information to include in investigational new drug applications (INDs) to support the use of 
individual cohorts; (3) when to interact with FDA on planning and conduct of multiple expansion 
cohort trials; and (4) safeguards to protect subjects enrolled in FIH expansion cohort trials. 
This guidance does not address all issues relating to clinical trial design, statistical analysis, or 
the biomarker development process. Those topics are addressed in other guidances including the

ev_033.document_title: Expansion Cohorts: Use in First-in-Human Clinical Trials to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics
ev_033.quote:
Phase 1 clinical trials are designed to determine the metabolism and pharmacologic actions of an 
investigational drug in humans, the side effects associated with increasing doses, and, when 
conducted in patients rather than healthy subjects, to gain early evidence of effectiveness.4 The 
primary rationale for conducting phase 1 studies is to obtain sufficient information about the 
drug’s pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacologic effects to permit the design of subsequent well-
controlled, scientifically valid phase 2 studies. The number of subjects included in phase 1 trials 
is anticipated to be 20 to 80 subjects. 
FIH multiple expansion cohort trials are intended to expedite development by seamlessly 
proceeding from initial determination of a tolerated dose to assessments that are more typical of 
phase 2 trials (i.e., to estimate antitumor activity) within individual expansion cohorts. In 
general, these expansion cohorts will be initiated before the analysis of the metabolism and 
pharmacokinetics of the investigational drug and with limited safety assessment. Therefore, it is 
critical to ensure close and prompt monitoring for toxicity in expanded cohorts, given that such

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: 50–750 mg 1일 1회 투여 범위만 제시되며 용량별 노출 또는 노출–반응 자료는 없다. 따라서 초록은 자체 용량 선정 근거를 평가할 자료를 제공하지 않는다.

T05_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: 59명 증량 후 MTD에서 71명 확대했다는 초록은 하위 용량 비교, DLT·증량 기준, 코호트 근거·중단 규칙, PK 채혈 및 용량 조정 규칙을 제시하지 않는다. 이를 실제 프로토콜에 없었다고 단정할 수 없으며, 제시된 자료만으로 자체 용량 선정 근거를 뒷받침하기 어렵다.

T06_analog_trial.position: 크리조티닙 치료 중 진행한 환자의 치료 전 생검은 기술되어 있지만, 이전 치료 종료부터 DV-R03 시작까지의 간격은 제시되지 않는다. 잔여 독성·상호작용 관리의 적절성은 판단할 수 없다.

T00_protocol_scan.position: ‘400 mg 이상’ 환자 114명의 통합 반응률은 750 mg과 하위 용량의 편익–위험을 구분하지 못한다. 또한 자료는 2014년 발표 초록을 바탕으로 작성된 시놉시스이므로, 설계 안전장치가 실제로 없었다고 단정할 수 없다.

review_questions.hypothesis: The structure may have been classified as containing a reactive warhead without chemical evidence; structure alone cannot establish organ-specific toxicity.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Check the chemical structure against curated compound and bioactivity records; distinguish measured potency and reactivity from structural inference.
review_questions.search_query: ChEMBL compound structure ALK inhibitor bioactivity reactive warhead evidence

review_questions.hypothesis: Class-associated toxicities may not have been addressed in the available safety description.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Compare ALK-inhibitor labeling and evidence available by April 2014 with the reported adverse events; establish whether the unavailable protocol contained relevant monitoring.
review_questions.protocol_span: DV-R03 is an oral small molecule (ALK tyrosine kinase receptor inhibitor).
review_questions.search_query: FDA ALK inhibitor prescribing information warnings precautions monitoring 2014

review_questions.hypothesis: The reported assessment of safety may omit monitoring for clinically important class-label risks.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve contemporaneous US labels and the full protocol, if obtainable; compare specified ECG, liver-test, pulmonary, and other monitoring schedules rather than treating an abstract’s silence as proof of omission.
review_questions.protocol_span: Patients were assessed to determine the safety, pharmacokinetic properties, and antitumor activity of DV-R03.
review_questions.search_query: FDA crizotinib prescribing information 2014 QT prolongation hepatotoxicity pneumonitis monitoring

review_questions.hypothesis: The abstract does not supply dose-specific exposure or exposure–response evidence sufficient to assess the selected dose.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain the original PK tables, exposure variability, dose proportionality, and exposure–efficacy/toxicity analyses; do not substitute another product’s label PK for DV-R03 measurements.
review_questions.protocol_span: Methods: In this phase 1 study, we administered oral DV-R03 in doses of 50 to 750 mg once daily to patients with advanced cancers harboring genetic alterations in ALK.
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dose optimization guidance exposure response efficacy safety pharmacokinetic dose selection final

review_questions.hypothesis: Selecting the MTD for expansion may have bypassed comparison with lower, potentially effective and better-tolerated doses.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Look for dose-level comparisons of efficacy, exposure, chronic tolerability, and dose interruptions supporting 750 mg; distinguish standards applicable in 2014 from later FDA final guidance.
review_questions.protocol_span: In an expansion phase of the study, patients received the maximum tolerated dose.
review_questions.search_query: FDA Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases final guidance MTD dose comparison applicability

review_questions.hypothesis: The escalation report does not establish whether DLT assessment and escalation decisions were statistically adequate.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain cohort sizes by dose, DLT window and definitions, escalation algorithm, target toxicity rate, and late-toxicity handling; check the contemporaneous governing standard.
review_questions.protocol_span: Results: A total of 59 patients were enrolled in the dose-escalation phase. The maximum tolerated dose of DV-R03 was 750 mg once daily; dose-limiting toxic events included diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, elevated aminotransferase levels, and hypophosphatemia.
review_questions.search_query: FDA phase 1 oncology clinical trials dose escalation DLT cohort size late toxicity guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: The 71-patient expansion may have lacked prespecified cohort rationale, sample size, or safety stopping rules.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Find the expansion protocol and amendments specifying population, objectives, statistical precision, accrual rationale, and stopping boundaries; account for the 2014 study date.
review_questions.protocol_span: This phase was followed by an expansion phase, in which an additional 71 patients were treated, for a total of 130 patients overall.
review_questions.search_query: FDA expansion cohorts first in human clinical trials oncology drugs guidance objectives sample size stopping rules date issued

review_questions.hypothesis: The abstract does not establish whether PK sampling captured exposure relevant to once-daily dosing and accumulation.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve sampling times, steady-state and food-effect assessments, metabolite measurements, and PK variability; assess against guidance applicable to the study period.
review_questions.protocol_span: Patients were assessed to determine the safety, pharmacokinetic properties, and antitumor activity of DV-R03.
review_questions.search_query: FDA phase 1 oncology pharmacokinetic sampling steady state accumulation dose selection guidance

review_questions.hypothesis: Dose-modification rules for the reported serious dose-limiting toxicities are not ascertainable from the abstract.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain the protocol’s interruption, reduction, rechallenge, and discontinuation criteria for gastrointestinal toxicity, dehydration, liver enzyme elevations, and hypophosphatemia.
review_questions.protocol_span: dose-limiting toxic events included diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, elevated aminotransferase levels, and hypophosphatemia.
review_questions.search_query: ICH E6 protocol stopping rules dose adjustment toxicity investigational drug clinical trial

review_questions.hypothesis: Eligibility may not have specified a sufficient washout from prior ALK therapy to separate residual toxicity and drug interactions.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Obtain the actual eligibility criteria and washout intervals; compare contemporaneous analogous trials and prior-drug pharmacokinetics without treating analog designs as binding requirements.
review_questions.protocol_span: Tumor biopsies were performed before DV-R03 treatment to identify resistance mutations in ALK in a group of patients with NSCLC who had had disease progression during treatment with crizotinib.
review_questions.search_query: ALK inhibitor phase 1 trial crizotinib prior therapy washout eligibility 2014

review_questions.hypothesis: Pooling all patients receiving at least 400 mg may obscure dose-specific benefit–risk differences relevant to choosing 750 mg.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Retrieve response, exposure, toxicity, and follow-up by individual dose, including lower doses; determine whether the pooled analysis supports or undermines the selected dose.
review_questions.protocol_span: Among 114 patients with NSCLC who received at least 400 mg of DV-R03 per day, the overall response rate was 58% (95% confidence interval [CI], 48 to 67).
review_questions.search_query: FDA oncology dosage optimization final guidance evaluate efficacy safety at multiple doses exposure response

review_questions.hypothesis: Treating this published abstract as the complete protocol could create unsupported findings of missing design safeguards.
review_questions.what_to_verify: Seek the original protocol, amendments, and study report; distinguish absent source material from a confirmed design omission, and avoid applying post-2014 guidance retroactively.
